text:
A DECLARATION OF NON-COMPLIANCE

By: Jason Gray

2026•11•05 (6026 A.L.)
0724 (GMT-6)

To the system that taught humanity obedience before it ever taught us freedom.

FUCK YOU.

To the institutions that convinced generations of human beings that their worth could be measured by their productivity, their bank accounts, their possessions, and their willingness to surrender their lives in exchange for the privilege of surviving.

FUCK YOU.

To the governments that manufacture division, sell fear as protection, and demand loyalty from the very people they repeatedly betray.

To the corporations that have turned human suffering into a business model, sickness into revenue, war into an industry, and debt into a generational inheritance.

To the financial institutions that collect billions upon billions in interest while entire families work themselves into early graves trying to repay obligations that seem designed never to disappear.

FUCK YOU.

To the education systems that too often reward memorization over imagination, compliance over curiosity, and conformity over independent thought.

To the religious authorities that have used the promise of salvation and the threat of eternal punishment to exercise power over the human conscience.

To every institution that has ever convinced a human being that questioning authority is dangerous, that disobedience is immoral, or that thinking independently is somehow a threat to civilization.

FUCK YOU.

While we are at it, let us address something that humanity has been conditioned to avoid discussing.

The entire arrangement.

The whole fucking thing.

From the moment a human being enters this world, the machinery begins.

Before you can speak, you are registered.

Before you can reason, you are categorized.

Before you can question, you are instructed.

Before you understand what freedom means, you are taught what obedience looks like.

You are given a nationality, an economic position, a collection of inherited beliefs, and an identity shaped by institutions that existed long before you arrived, and somewhere along the way, you are expected to believe that all of this constitutes freedom.

You are told to work hard.

To follow the rules.

To respect authority.

To borrow responsibly.

To pay your taxes.

To contribute to society.

To save for retirement.

To trust the experts.

To trust the institutions.

To trust the process, and above all, to stop asking so many fucking questions, because apparently the greatest threat to a civilization that claims to value freedom is a human being who actually intends to exercise it.

FUCK YOU.

You have spent centuries constructing a world where people are born into obligations they never agreed to, assigned identities they never chose, and taught to compete against one another for resources that should never have been used as instruments of domination.

You divided humanity by race.

By religion.

By nationality.

By political affiliation.

By wealth.

By social status.

By every conceivable distinction you could amplify until human beings forgot how much they had in common, and then you stood above those divisions, presenting yourselves as the only ones capable of maintaining order.

You convinced the poor to hate the poor.

You convinced workers to blame other workers.

You convinced nations to fear other nations.

You convinced human beings that strangers on the other side of imaginary borders were their enemies, while industries profiting from hostility continued operating without interruption.

You took the natural human instinct to protect family and community and redirected it into suspicion, hostility, and endless competition.

You taught people to defend institutions that would replace them tomorrow without a second thought.

You taught them to identify with political parties that routinely disappoint them.

You taught them to celebrate economic growth while ignoring the destruction occurring beneath the numbers, and perhaps your greatest achievement was convincing humanity that this arrangement was normal.

That endless economic expansion on a finite planet was reasonable.

That perpetual indebtedness was prosperity.

That exhaustion was ambition.

That obedience was virtue.

That freedom meant choosing between options someone else had already selected.

That spending the overwhelming majority of a human lifetime working simply to remain alive was the natural order of existence.

FUCK YOU.

Let us talk about money.

That extraordinary invention that was supposed to facilitate human exchange and somehow became the central authority governing almost every aspect of human existence.

A system where money can be created through lending, where interest accumulates, where wealth concentrates, and where the people producing the actual goods and services frequently struggle to afford the very things they create.

Where governments borrow enormous sums, service the resulting debt, and pass the obligations to generations that have not yet been born.

Where entire populations are told that essential services are unaffordable while staggering amounts of capital continue circulating through financial markets, military procurement, corporate subsidies, and speculative investments.

Where a human being can spend forty years working, pay hundreds of thousands in taxes and interest, and still arrive at retirement wondering whether they can afford to remain in their own home.

We call this progress.

We call this prosperity.

We call this civilization.

What an extraordinary fucking achievement.

You have managed to convince billions of people that survival must be purchased from the very economic structures they spend their lives maintaining, and whenever someone questions the arrangement, the response is almost always the same.

That is just how the world works.

No.

That is how the world has been organized.

There is a difference, and it is a difference that matters more than almost anything else humanity could possibly understand, because something created by human decisions can be changed by human decisions.

Your rules are not the laws of physics.

Your economic theories are not commandments written into the fabric of the universe.

Your institutions are not eternal.

Your hierarchies are not sacred, and your authority is not evidence of your moral superiority.

FUCK YOU.

Now let us talk about war.

The great industrial enterprise of organized human destruction.

The machinery that turns fear into funding, political ambition into military campaigns, and the deaths of ordinary human beings into statistics presented at press conferences.

How many generations have been taught that the people living somewhere else are fundamentally different?

How many young men and women have been sent to kill people they had never met, in countries they had never visited, over conflicts they barely understood?

How many families have buried their children beneath flags while the people responsible for the decisions continued attending meetings, delivering speeches, and collecting salaries?

How many fortunes have been made manufacturing the equipment required to destroy what other human beings spent generations building, and how many times have the same institutions that failed to prevent catastrophe presented themselves as the only legitimate authorities capable of rebuilding what was destroyed?

The soldier on one side wants to return home.

The soldier on the other side wants exactly the same thing.

The mother on one side prays for her child.

The mother on the other side does too.

The ordinary human beings caught between competing powers often have more in common with one another than with the leaders demanding their sacrifice, yet we continue allowing geography, ideology, and inherited hostility to determine who deserves our compassion, and when someone suggests that perhaps the machinery itself deserves examination, they are accused of being naive.

Unpatriotic.

Dangerous.

Disloyal.

As though questioning the political and economic incentives behind organized violence is somehow more offensive than the violence itself.

FUCK YOU.

Do not misunderstand me.

I am not condemning every person who works within an institution.

I am not condemning the nurse, the teacher, the soldier, the public servant, the tradesperson, or the ordinary worker trying to provide for a family.

Those people are humanity.

They are the ones keeping the world functioning.

I am condemning the structures that exploit their dedication, manipulate their loyalties, and treat their lives as expendable resources.

I am condemning the belief that institutions deserve unquestioning obedience merely because they possess authority.

I am condemning the extraordinary arrogance of anyone who believes that occupying a position of power grants them ownership over another human being’s conscience, and I am condemning the culture of fear that encourages people to remain silent when they know something is wrong, because silence has become one of the most valuable commodities in the modern world.

Not the silence of peace.

The silence of resignation.

The silence of people who have learned that speaking openly can cost them their employment, their reputation, their social standing, or their access to the communities upon which they depend.

The silence of people who look around, recognize contradictions, and decide that survival requires pretending not to see them, and eventually that silence becomes so widespread that the absence of opposition is mistaken for consent.

Well, you do not have mine.

Not now.

Not tomorrow.

Not ever.

I have lived long enough to understand that approval is not the same thing as truth.

That popularity is not the same thing as integrity.

That institutional recognition is not the same thing as wisdom, and that a person can spend an entire lifetime being praised for following instructions while never once examining whether those instructions deserved to be followed.

I have absolutely no interest in living that way.

I have no interest in spending whatever remains of my existence pretending that the world makes sense simply because acknowledging its contradictions makes other people uncomfortable.

I have no interest in protecting the reputations of institutions that refuse to examine their own failures, and I have no interest in apologizing for asking questions that should have been asked generations ago.

Which brings me to something else.

To anyone who finds these words offensive.

To anyone who believes that questioning authority is an act of betrayal.

To anyone who thinks that criticizing the machinery of government, finance, religion, media, or institutional power should somehow disqualify a human being from participating in society.

To anyone who would rather silence a question than answer it.

If you do not like what I have to say, you are free to disagree, but you will not silence me.

Come and explain exactly which part of independent thought frightens you.

Come and explain why your authority should exist beyond scrutiny.

Come and explain why human dignity should remain subordinate to economic interests.

Come and explain why ordinary people must continually sacrifice while those at the top so frequently escape accountability.

Come and explain why freedom of expression is celebrated in principle but treated as an inconvenience whenever someone says something uncomfortable.

Come and explain why the people demanding transparency from everyone else so often resist it themselves.

Come and explain why institutions that insist upon public trust become defensive when the public begins asking difficult questions.

Come and explain why the answer to systemic failure is so often another demand for patience, another promise of reform, another committee, another election, another generation of waiting.

I am right here.

I am not hiding behind anonymity.

I am not asking anyone to fight on my behalf.

I am not threatening anyone with violence.

I am exercising the very freedom that every supposedly civilized society claims to defend, and if that is enough to make me a problem in your eyes?

THEN FUCK YOU TOO.

I will not surrender my conscience to protect your comfort.

I will not dilute my words to preserve your illusion of authority.

I will not pretend that injustice becomes acceptable because it has been institutionalized, and I will not confuse your disapproval with evidence that I am wrong.

You are welcome to disagree.

You are welcome to challenge every sentence.

You are welcome to present evidence, arguments, and perspectives that contradict my own.

That is what genuine freedom of thought requires, but intimidation is not an argument.

Censorship is not a rebuttal.

Ridicule is not evidence, and authority is not a substitute for truth.

If you want a discussion, bring one.

If you want accountability, practice it.

If you want respect, demonstrate that you understand what respect means, but if your only response to uncomfortable questions is an attempt to silence the person asking them, then you have already demonstrated precisely why those questions needed to be asked.

FUCK YOU.

Let me address the people who will inevitably misunderstand this declaration.

This is not a call for violence.

This is not a declaration of war against ordinary people.

This is not an invitation to replace one oppressive structure with another.

It is a refusal to accept that the current organization of human civilization represents the highest expression of what our species can accomplish.

It is a refusal to accept that exploitation is inevitable.

That poverty is necessary.

That war is permanent.

That division is natural.

That compassion is weakness.

That humanity must remain trapped within institutions simply because previous generations failed to imagine alternatives.

The most dangerous idea to a system dependent upon unquestioning obedience is not violence.

Violence is something systems already understand.

They have departments for it.

Budgets for it.

Training programs for it.

Weapons for it.

Entire industries built around it.

What they struggle to accommodate is a population that begins questioning the assumptions upon which their authority depends.

A population that refuses to be divided by manufactured hostility.

A population that demands evidence instead of slogans.

A population that recognizes that political allegiance does not require intellectual surrender.

A population that understands the difference between respecting the law and believing every law is just.

A population that refuses to treat economic productivity as the measure of human worth.

A population that begins placing human well being above the endless accumulation of wealth.

A population that stops confusing the preservation of institutions with the preservation of civilization.

That is the revolution worth having.

Not another flag.

Not another political party.

Not another charismatic leader promising salvation.

Not another ideology demanding absolute loyalty.

Not another hierarchy with a different name.

Something far more profound.

A fundamental reconsideration of what humanity is doing here.

Why we organize our societies the way we do.

Why we tolerate conditions that cause widespread suffering.

Why we continue repeating historical failures while congratulating ourselves on technological advancement.

Why we have developed extraordinary capabilities for manipulating matter, transmitting information, and accumulating wealth, yet remain so remarkably unsuccessful at ensuring that every human being has access to the basic conditions necessary for a dignified existence.

We can communicate across the planet instantaneously.

We can explore distant worlds.

We can manipulate atoms.

We can construct machines capable of processing information at extraordinary speeds.

We can map the human genome.

We can build technologies that would have appeared supernatural to previous generations, yet millions of people still struggle to obtain food, shelter, medical care, and basic security, and we are expected to believe that the principal obstacle is a lack of human capability.

No.

The obstacle is also found in our priorities.

Our incentives.

Our distribution of resources.

Our willingness to tolerate suffering when eliminating it would interfere with established arrangements.

We have built a civilization capable of extraordinary achievements while continuing to organize enormous portions of human existence around fear, scarcity, competition, and domination, and somehow we have been conditioned to celebrate the achievements without questioning the contradictions.

FUCK YOU.

I am tired of watching human beings apologize for existing.

Tired of watching people measure their lives against standards established by industries that profit from their insecurity.

Tired of watching families disintegrate under economic pressure.

Tired of watching children inherit a world of obligations before they have had an opportunity to understand what those obligations mean.

Tired of watching people work themselves into physical and emotional exhaustion while being told that their suffering is evidence of personal inadequacy.

Tired of watching compassion dismissed as impractical.

Tired of watching cruelty disguised as strength.

Tired of watching political theatre replace meaningful accountability.

Tired of watching human beings become so accustomed to dysfunction that they defend it as tradition, and I am especially tired of being told that recognizing these things makes someone negative.

No.

Recognizing suffering is not negativity.

Questioning injustice is not extremism.

Demanding accountability is not hatred.

Refusing to participate in manufactured hostility is not weakness, and believing humanity can create something better is not delusion.

It is the beginning of responsibility, because once you recognize that a structure is harming people, you have a decision to make.

You can continue defending it.

You can remain silent, or you can begin asking what it would take to change it, and no, change will not arrive simply because someone writes an angry declaration.

Words alone will not feed the hungry.

Words alone will not end wars.

Words alone will not dismantle exploitative incentives.

Words alone will not create justice, but words can expose contradictions.

They can challenge assumptions.

They can interrupt inherited patterns of thinking.

They can remind isolated individuals that they are not the only ones questioning what they have been told, and sometimes the beginning of meaningful change is nothing more complicated than someone finally saying what others have been afraid to say.

Without asking permission.

Without requesting approval.

Without apologizing for the discomfort that follows.

So here it is.

TO THE SYSTEM...FUCK YOU.

To the culture that values profit above people.

FUCK YOU.

To the machinery that turns human suffering into political advantage.

FUCK YOU.

To the industries that benefit from perpetual conflict.

FUCK YOU.

To the institutions that demand accountability from ordinary citizens while resisting accountability themselves.

FUCK YOU.

To the people who exploit fear, manipulate division, and convince humanity that its greatest enemies are other ordinary human beings.

FUCK YOU.

To anyone who believes that wealth makes them inherently superior.

To anyone who believes that poverty makes another human being disposable.

To anyone who believes that authority places them beyond criticism.

To anyone who believes that another person’s freedom of conscience exists only with their permission.

FUCK YOU.

To those who are offended by the language?

Good.

Now ask yourselves why four letters offend you more than the suffering being described.

Why an expression of anger attracts more outrage than the conditions that produced it.

Why the demand for politeness so often becomes a convenient way to avoid confronting uncomfortable truths.

I am not writing this to be polite.

I am writing it because there comes a point when polite language becomes inadequate to express the magnitude of what needs to be examined.

I am not seeking permission to speak.

I am not campaigning for anyone’s approval.

I am not interested in becoming another acceptable voice repeating acceptable opinions within acceptable boundaries.

I am a human being.

I have lived.

I have worked.

I have suffered.

I have made mistakes.

I have watched people I love suffer.

I have watched institutions fail people who depended upon them, and I have reached a point in my life where the prospect of being disliked for speaking openly concerns me considerably less than the prospect of remaining silent about what I believe matters.

I do not claim to possess every answer.

I do not claim that every suspicion is a fact.

I do not claim that every institution is corrupt or that every person exercising authority is malicious, but I do claim the right to question all of them.

To examine their actions.

To challenge their assumptions.

To demand evidence.

To revise my own conclusions when the facts require it, and to refuse the idea that any human created system is entitled to unconditional allegiance.

That right does not belong to a government.

It does not belong to a corporation.

It does not belong to a religious institution.

It does not belong to a political movement.

It belongs to the human being exercising it, and I will exercise mine.

Until my final breath.

Not because I believe I am above anyone else, but because I refuse to place anyone else above the fundamental dignity of being human.

If you disagree with me, disagree.

If you believe I am wrong, demonstrate why.

If you have a better argument, present it.

If you believe that your position, your title, your money, your institutional influence, or your political authority gives you the right to determine what I am permitted to think or say?

YOU ARE MISTAKEN.

Bring your arguments.

Bring your evidence.

Bring every justification you have for the world you insist must remain exactly as it is.

I will listen.

I will question.

I will not be intimidated into silence, because I have absolutely no intention of spending the remainder of my existence pretending that obedience is freedom.

If that offends you?

If that threatens your carefully maintained image of authority?

If that makes you uncomfortable because someone has finally refused to participate in the collective performance?

THEN FUCK YOU TOO.

I am not here to destroy humanity.

I am here to remind humanity that it deserves better than the endless repetition of its own suffering.

I am not here to manufacture another enemy.

I am here to question why we have been taught to manufacture enemies at all.

I am not here to demand that everyone think as I do.

I am here to defend the right of every human being to think without coercion, and I am not here to replace the system with another system that simply changes the names of those holding power.

I am here to challenge the assumption that power itself should remain beyond meaningful scrutiny, because humanity does not belong to its governments.

Humanity does not belong to its corporations.

Humanity does not belong to its banks.

Humanity does not belong to its religions.

Humanity does not belong to its political parties, and humanity certainly does not belong to the machinery that has convinced so many people that their only purpose is to keep that machinery operating.

Humanity belongs to itself, and the most important realization of all is that the system has never been some supernatural force operating beyond human understanding.

It was constructed.

It was maintained.

It was normalized, and it can be reconsidered.

Not through blind rage.

Not through indiscriminate destruction.

Not through the creation of another class of enemies, but through awareness, courage, cooperation, accountability, and the refusal to continue mistaking inherited arrangements for immutable reality.

The moment people stop believing that things must remain as they are is the moment alternatives become possible, and that is where meaningful change begins.

Not with another master.

Not with another saviour.

Not with another promise that someone else will eventually fix everything, but with human beings recognizing their own responsibility to one another.

This is my declaration.

I will not hate another human being because a government tells me to.

Through it all, I have made it my goal to stay connected to the faithful here on Christian Twitter. You have seen my daily posts about where I believe AI is ultimately heading and the people running point on the transhumanist agenda.

I probably don’t come across as a trained theologian, but I do hold a theological degree. My rants and musings arise from Scripture. Behind them are years of study, writing, speaking, and research.

I needed to know whether this perspective was defensible. Could it withstand close examination of the biblical text? Could it answer serious objections? Did it hold together theologically?

After years of testing it, I am convinced it does.

What is my view?

The Beast of Revelation is the final global governing order, powered by Superintelligence.

The False Prophet is the human Antichrist that represents the final order, speaks like the dragon, and exercises all of its authority.

The Mark of the Beast is a brain-computer interface that integrates human beings into the system.

Those who have followed me over the years know this is my perspective. Now, for the first time, I have brought the full argument together in a book:

Techno-Futurist Eschatological Perspective:
An Exegetical and Theological Reassessment of the Beast, Antichrist, and the End of the Age.

This is a serious, technically demanding, scholarly theological treatise. I examine the passages, address competing interpretations, and defend the case that this perspective offers greater exegetical and theological coherence than the conventional framework popularized by the Left Behind series.

I present this work to you before God.  I have done my best.

I challenge you to read it with your Bible open. Test the argument.

The purpose reaches beyond winning a theological debate. The saints must recognize deception, endure opposition, and remain faithful to Jesus Christ.

This is my attempt to echo heaven's commands:
1. Believe in the Lord Jesus and be saved.
2. Do not be seduced by Babylon. Come out of her.
3. Do not worship the Beast or receive its mark.

May heaven and earth bear witness today: I have blown the trumpet as loudly and clearly as I know how.

The culprit is electromagnetic radiation leaking from the HDMI cable

HDMI sends video as rapidly changing electrical signals. Those signals produce electromagnetic emissions around the cable and its connectors

An antenna can pick up some of that radiation, while a software-defined radio (SDR) such as a HackRF captures and converts it into data a computer can process

Software called TempestSDR can then synchronise the captured signal and reconstruct a rough representation of the screen

This is a form of electromagnetic side-channel attack, commonly associated with the name TEMPEST

Researchers have since taken the technique further with Deep-TEMPEST

Instead of relying only on conventional signal processing, they trained a neural network to map the degraded radio signal back to the original screen image

Their experiments improved text recognition error rates by more than 60 percentage points compared with earlier implementations

The research used an SDR, an antenna and a computer running open-source software. It also included more than 1,300 real-world signal captures

This isn't a remote attack that lets someone anywhere in the world watch your monitor. The attacker needs suitable radio equipment, proximity to the target and favourable signal conditions

But it demonstrates an unusual security problem: information can escape through physical emissions even when the device has no network connection

The main bottleneck used to be syncing it your signal but Tempest already fixes that
